findings.result_name: v14:prop-fv-stall — "the few-denominator class contains stalls" is a category error under the paper's own def:decision-rule
findings.defect: def:decision-rule declares a rule NON-STALLING if it returns bot only when w*(v^(0))=w*(v^(1)) for EVERY controlled vertex. On FV(n) every controlled vertex has two successors of equal value (prop:fv-family proves this). Abstaining on FV(n) is therefore precisely what a sound non-stalling rule is licensed to do. FV(n) places no obstruction whatever on the existence of a sound non-stalling decision rule, so it is not a stall in the paper's technical sense, and the proposition's title "The few-denominator class contains stalls" should not be written. The integrated text does add the vacuity caveat, but the title and the opening sentence still assert the contrary.
findings.evidence: frontier.tex def:decision-rule (non-stalling clause) against prop:fv-family ("every controlled vertex ... has two successors of equal value, so no controlled vertex is value-distinguishing"). Further, FV defeats neither M1 nor M3: on FV every sigma has S_sigma = empty, so thm:seed-dichotomy's hypothesis holds at every sigma and the M3 seed is exact. So as a stalling family FV is strictly weaker than WD(e,j,m), which defeats M2, M2T, M4, M5 AND M6 at value-distinguishing vertices with an unconditional 2^{Omega(N)} count (rem:wedge, thm:wedge-proved). The route's headline "item (6) is answered in the NEGATIVE" oversells a family that is weaker than one the paper already has.

verdict:
Blunt answer: this route is a competent verification pass wrapped around a significance claim that does not survive contact with the paper. About half of what it offers is already in frontier.tex, a quarter is subsumed, and its one headline discovery is misframed and carries a false clause that has already been integrated.

IS IT NEW? Four of the eleven items the route says \"INTEGRATE as they stand\" are not new. deg:prop-hk5 IS prop:hkfive (integrated 13 minutes after the route's last write). deg:prop-g6 IS rem:flat's ceiling, which already credits \"a later verification route's\" search — this one. cor:prec-characterisation IS rem:escape-rate's final paragraph, which already states the characterisation AND attributes the hard direction to Blondel–Nesterov AND says it is not elementary; the route re-labels it \"proved\" on an argument that is wrong as written (counterexample above). deg:prop-nondeg4 is subsumed by rem:hk-survey — I canonicalised its outmap and it is one of the 56 Holt–Klee height-6 classes rem:hk-survey already realises nondegenerately at about 100 vertices, against the route's 253. Unflagged prior art: T-hat in the precondition block is the censored/stochastically-complemented chain (Meyer, already on the DEAD list) and the two-sided rounded iteration is Haddad–Monmege (already on the prior-art list); the route flags neither. It does correctly flag Blondel–Nesterov, which is to its credit.

IS IT CIRCULAR OR VACUOUS? The FV result is vacuous in the paper's own technical sense, not merely \"vacuous\" in the informal sense the route concedes. def:decision-rule's non-stalling clause EXPLICITLY licenses abstention when every controlled vertex has equal successor values — which is FV's defining property. So FV(n) is not a stall; it is the case the definition carves out. \"The few-denominator class DOES contain stalls\" must not be written, and the proposition now in the paper is titled exactly that. FV also defeats neither M1 nor M3 (S_sigma is empty at every sigma, so thm:seed-dichotomy applies at once), making it strictly weaker than WD, which defeats M2, M2T, M4, M5, M6 at value-distinguishing vertices with a proved 2^{Omega(N)} count. The contracted class is a claimed polynomial class with no exhibited member outside the six, and the route's own prop:prec-wedge puts the wedge outside it, so it cannot reach the frontier either. No claimed barrier here covers any of M1–M6 or def:bsi.

IS THE VERIFICATION HONEST? Mostly yes on the arithmetic, and the exact-rational discipline is real. But three reported statements are contradicted by the route's own artefacts. (i) \"M5 decides every controlled vertex at round two or three\" — fv.out and fv3.out record None at every vertex of FV(4) and FV(5); I re-ran it and the minimum own-successor entry on FV(4) is 1, 1/4, 1/20, 1/100, 1/500, 1/2500 over six rounds with nothing firing. That false clause is now in frontier.tex's prop:fv-stall and must be struck. (ii) \"all 27 parts terminate with maximum 21\" — g6_11.out is empty and three shards report 20. (iii) las2:prop-cyc-rlt's lambda_0 hypothesis is reported as corroborated by a table showing infeasibility at every lambda tested up to 63/64, far above lambda_0. And the M1 clause the paper now carries has no computation behind it anywhere in the route's directory. cor:prec-characterisation rests on random sampling over 120 games of three to seven non-sinks, which by this project's own standing rule is not evidence.

THE REAL REMAINING GAP, stated harder than the route states it. The route's gap (\"whether the few-denominator class contains a non-vacuous stall\") is softer than the truth in two ways. Precisely: exhibit a stopping SSG with D(G) = poly(N) carrying a value-distinguishing controlled vertex at which the Z-seeded own-successor test of the transport–slack hybrid is silent for superpolynomially many rounds, or prove that 1/D(G) >= 1/poly(N) forces the two-sided value-iteration width below the gap in poly(N) rounds — and note that the second disjunct, if true, would put SSG-Value in P on the whole class by thm:slack-vi-upper, so it is not a lemma anyone should expect to be easy. Separately and more usefully, the route leaves untouched the one question its own best item raises: whether a genuinely two-player, non-self-dual, track-coupled family exists on which BSI's round count grows — which prop:selfdual now narrows and rem:bsi-gap already frames.

BETTER OR WORSE? As submitted, integrating the whole thing makes the paper WORSE: roughly nine pages, of which four items are duplicates or subsumed, four more expand the Lasserre route the paper has already closed negatively and bounded in significance (rem:lasserre: \"it is evidence that it is weak already where the problem is easy\"), and the flagship item carries a false clause and a title the paper's own definitions forbid.

INTEGRATE: bsr:prop-selfdual (as a corollary of lem:duality, with the caveat that MR is still uncovered by every barrier, so self-dual games are reduced, not excluded) and bsr:prop-normal — the two genuinely new, genuinely useful items, and the two the root did NOT take. Also the las2:thm-two sentence, folded into rem:lasserre as \"and the lift is exact on every one of them\", replacing the current \"touches none of them\"; and the route's four repairs, all of which are correct: the Q_16 vertex count, the deleted hypothesis in cor:selfread, the two formula errors and the killed \"iff\" reading in las2:thm-cyc, and the missing log kappa-hat plus doubling schedule in thm:prec-contract-class.

DO NOT INTEGRATE: deg:prop-hk5 (= prop:hkfive), deg:prop-g and deg:prop-g6 (= rem:flat, already credited to this route), deg:prop-nondeg4 (subsumed by rem:hk-survey — and it is already in the paper as prop:nondeg-overshoot, where it should be cut or reduced to a footnote), cor:prec-characterisation (= rem:escape-rate, with a broken proof), thm:prec-contract-class as a class (no member outside the six; and attribute Meyer and Haddad–Monmege before anything from that block goes in), and the las2 CYC/RLT block until CYC is built as an actual SSG and the lambda_0 framing is reconciled with its own table.

FIX IMMEDIATELY, in the paper as it now stands: strike \"and the seeded hybrid of \\Cref{sec:hybrid} does so by round three\" from prop:fv-stall — it is false at n=4 — and either verify or strike the M1 clause beside it; retitle prop:fv-stall so it does not assert a stall that def:decision-rule licenses; and add one line to prop:nondeg-overshoot recording that its orientation class is one of rem:hk-survey's 56 and is already realised there in a hundred vertices.
